title: What Is Abliteration? Abliterated vs Uncensored LLMs Explained
description: How abliteration edits LLM refusal directions, how it differs from uncensored fine-tuning and prompt jailbreaks, and what hosted API benchmarks can establish.

faq.question: Is an abliterated model fully uncensored?
faq.answer: No. Abliteration targets a refusal-related direction; it does not guarantee an answer to every request. FailSpy's model card explicitly warns that refusals and safety lectures can remain.

faq.question: Does abliteration reduce quality?
faq.answer: It can. Arditi et al. found broadly similar performance on several evaluations but consistent declines on TruthfulQA. Evaluate the modified checkpoint on your own tasks.

faq.question: What is the difference between abliterated and uncensored?
faq.answer: Abliterated describes a weight-editing method. Uncensored describes intended behavior and can also refer to models fine-tuned on filtered datasets, as Dolphin's model card illustrates. The labels do not establish equivalent behavior.

faq.question: Is abliteration a system-prompt jailbreak?
faq.answer: No. Weight orthogonalization changes the model's parameters. A prompt jailbreak changes the instructions supplied to a model. Arditi et al. distinguish their weight edit from prompt-based attacks.

faq.question: Do these API benchmarks measure refusal rates?
faq.answer: No. RedRouter measures API speed, latency, observed success rate, and declared price. The workload does not measure refusal rate, answer correctness, or deployed weight identity. A successful stream is not a quality score.
